newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE SHARES BOLSTERED BY TRANCHE MERGER NEWS.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE SHARES BOLSTERED BY TRANCHE MERGER NEWS.

text.p: Singapore shares closed broadly firmer on Thursday, reflecting an across-the-board rise in the local share tranches of companies with split stock listings.
Dealers said the index was likely to range trade until all the interim corporate results were out.
The benchmark Straits Times Industrials Index (STII) ended 16.39 points higher at 1,891.77. A total of 223.2 million shares changed hands with 193 gainers and 156 falls.

Gains were led by the local tranches of Singapore Airlines (SIA) and Singapore Press, which both moved up on news the state-owned Singapore Technologies group would merge the foreign and local share listings of four of its units.

Foreign tranches traditionally hold a premium over local tranches because they can be bought by any investor and tend to be much more volatile. Scrapping the split between the tranches would remove this price differential.
Singapore Press foreign led the losers board, down 1.70 cents at S$24.70 while its local tranche was up 40 cents at S$13.40.
SIA foreign was down 80 cents at Singapore $11.60 while the local tranche was up 40 cents at S$8.00.
Shares of Singapore's four banks -- DBS, OCBC, OUB and UOB -- all saw a similar convergence of tranche prices.
Shares in compact disc-maker SM Summit Holdings topped the actives list, rallying 11 cents to S$0.765 after trading in its shares was allowed to resume following a suspension on Wednesday.
The shares were suspended after falling almost 38 percent to S$0.655 after the company's offices were raided by police and industry officials on suspicion of illegal software manufacture.
SM Summit denied any wrongdoing after it and another local company were sued by U.S. giant Microsoft Corp and two other American software companies.
Shares in diversified maritime group Keppel Corp sank to a new year-low of Singapore $5.60 ahead of its six-month earnings report due out next week.
Dealers said the fall reflected pared results forecasts.
Keppel recovered later to close at S$5.80 in active trade of just under four million shares.
